exposure: Time interval from pregnancy onset to electrodiagnostic (EDx) examination
outcome: Clinical symptoms of CTS (e.g., bilateral and diurnal/permanent paraesthesia, symptom severity)
Electrophysiological abnormalities (e.g., conduction block (CB), classical test abnormalities)
cohort: The study included 130 women with pregnancy-related carpal tunnel syndrome (80 with onset during pregnancy, 50 after delivery), and a control group of 57 age-matched women with idiopathic carpal tunnel syndrome.
finding: Pregnancy-related Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (PRCTS) presents with more severe clinical symptoms and electrophysiological abnormalities, including a higher rate of conduction block, compared to idiopathic CTS, and corticosteroid injection is effective in improving clinical and EDx findings in most PRCTS cases.
followup_time: Up to 24 months after pregnancy onset for electrodiagnostic examination in the main cohort; follow-up after corticosteroid injection was also performed but its duration is not specified.
cross-section timing: Electrodiagnostic data was collected for 26 women during pregnancy and 104 women after delivery (83 within 6 months and 21 up to 24 months after pregnancy onset).
